h_{\left(i,+\infty\right)}\left(\mathbf y\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \inf_{\substack{r\in\mathbb Z\\r>i}}\frac{y_{\left(i,r\right)}}{r-i},\qquad
h_{\left(i,-\infty\right)}\left(\mathbf y\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \inf_{\substack{r\in\mathbb Z\\r<i}}\frac{y_{\left(i,r\right)}}{i-r}.
\]
Set $c_*=\delta/[2(1+R)]$. For each $b$ and $j$ there are integer
labels
\[
 \mathsf I^+_{b,j}\in\left[\widetilde m_{b-1/2}^{\,\mathsf K},
 \widetilde m_{b+1/2}^{\,\mathsf K}\right),\qquad
 \mathsf I^-_{b,j}\in\left(\widetilde m_{b-1/2}^{\,\mathsf K},
 \widetilde m_{b+1/2}^{\,\mathsf K}\right]
\]
such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ud-directed-seeds}
h_{\left(\mathsf I^+_{b,j},+\infty\right)}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf L}^{\min,j}\right)\geq c_*,
\qquad
h_{\left(\mathsf I^-_{b,j},-\infty\right)}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf L}^{\min,j}\right)\geq c_*.
\end{equation}
For completeness, consider the plus direction. A directed interval
beginning at the left endpoint of $A_{b,\mathsf K}$ and ending beyond its right
endpoint consists of complete blocks of total size $S$ and at most one
terminal block fragment of size $P$. By
\eqref{eq:ud-block-inf-lower}, the complete blocks have mass at least
$\delta S$, while \eqref{eq:ud-block-geometry} gives $P\leq RS$.
Thus every such directed average is at least
$\delta/(1+R)>c_*$. Lemma~4.4 of \cite{MR3568040}, with terminal
endpoint $+\infty$, gives $\mathsf I^+_{b,j}$. Reflection gives $\mathsf I^-_{b,j}$.
Choose the least admissible label in each of these finite blocks. The
conditions defining admissibility involve countably many measurable
averages, so $\mathsf I^{\pm}_{b,j}$ are random variables. These selected labels and
$c_*$ do not depend on $N$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 3: the exact finite summed-gap inequalities.}
Let $i_N^-\leq r<s\leq i_N^+$ be integers and let
$\mathbf z=(z_v)_{v\in\mathcal V_N}$ be a positive finite gap
configuration. Define
\begin{align}
\eta^{\mathrm{up}}_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(\mathbf z\right)
&\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \frac12\sum_{i=r+1}^{s}\frac1{z_{\left(r,i\right)}}
+\frac12\sum_{i=r}^{s-1}\frac1{z_{\left(i,s\right)}},
                                                        \label{eq:ud-eta-up}\\
\eta^{\mathrm{lw},N}_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(\mathbf z\right)
&\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \frac12\sum_{i=i_N^-}^{r-1}
\frac{z_{\left(r,s\right)}}{z_{\left(i,r\right)}z_{\left(i,s\right)}}
+\frac12\sum_{i=s+1}^{i_N^+}
\frac{z_{\left(r,s\right)}}{z_{\left(r,i\right)}z_{\left(s,i\right)}}.                  \label{eq:ud-eta-lw}
\end{align}
Empty sums are zero. If
$\mathbf z=\mathfrak q(\mathbf x)|_{\mathcal V_N}$ for a finite
particle configuration with label set $\mathcal I_N$, then telescoping
the particle drifts gives
\[
 \mu_s\left(\mathbf x\right)-\mu_r\left(\mathbf x\right)
 =2\left\{\eta^{\mathrm{up}}_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(\mathfrak q\left(\mathbf x\right)\right)
 -\eta^{\mathrm{lw},N}_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(\mathfrak q\left(\mathbf x\right)\right)\right\}.
\]
Indeed, the terms indexed by $r<i<s$ have positive sign, while an
exterior particle $i<r$ contributes
$-z_{(r,s)}/(z_{(i,r)}z_{(i,s)})$ and an exterior particle $i>s$
contributes $-z_{(r,s)}/(z_{(r,i)}z_{(s,i)})$.
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ud-finite-summed-gap}
\begin{split}
\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(u\right)-\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(u_0\right)
&=\left(\mathsf{B}_s\left(u\right)-\mathsf{B}_s\left(u_0\right)\right)
-\left(\mathsf{B}_r\left(u\right)-\mathsf{B}_r\left(u_0\right)\right)\\
&\quad+\beta\int_{u_0}^u
\left\{\eta^{\mathrm{up}}_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(w\right)\right)
-\eta^{\mathrm{lw},N}_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(w\right)\right)\right\}
\mathrm{d} w.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Both interactions in \eqref{eq:ud-eta-up}--\eqref{eq:ud-eta-lw} are
nonnegative. If $r=i_N^-$, the first sum in \eqref{eq:ud-eta-lw} is
absent; if $s=i_N^+$, the second is absent. Thus a physical endpoint
removes nonnegative summands from $\eta^{\mathrm{lw},N}$ and improves
the lower estimate from \eqref{eq:ud-finite-summed-gap};
$\eta^{\mathrm{up}}$ is unchanged.

Let $\mathcal C\subset\mathcal A=(r,s)\cap\mathbb{V}
\subset\mathcal V_N$ be intervals and, for $u_0\leq u\leq u_1$, put
\[
\mathsf O_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(u_0,u_1\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sup_{u_0\leq w\leq u_1}\left|\mathsf{B}_r\left(w\right)-\mathsf{B}_r\left(u_0\right)\right|
+\sup_{u_0\leq w\leq u_1}\left|\mathsf{B}_s\left(w\right)-\mathsf{B}_s\left(u_0\right)\right|.
\]
If $\mathcal A=(r,s)\cap\mathbb{V}$, we abbreviate
$\mathsf O_{\mathcal A}=\mathsf O_{(r,s)}$ and use the analogous
abbreviation for the two $\eta$'s.
For a finite $\mathcal D\subset\mathbb V$, we also write
$\mathsf{L}^{(N)}_{\mathcal D}=\sum_{v\in\mathcal D}\mathsf{L}_v^{(N)}$.
Rearrange \eqref{eq:ud-finite-summed-gap}, use
\eqref{eq:ud-Q-increment} on $\mathcal A\setminus\mathcal C$ for the
lower bound, and use positivity on that buffer for the upper bound.
All these inequalities are taken on the common full-probability event
for the countable choices of $N,r,s$ and the fixed time grid; continuity
then covers every $u$ in the relevant time interval.
For every $u_0\leq u\leq u_1$ this gives
\begin{subequations}\label{eq:ud-finite-summed-inequalities}
\begin{align}
\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\mathcal C}\left(u\right)
&\geq\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\mathcal C}\left(u_0\right)
-\beta\int_{u_0}^u\eta^{\mathrm{lw},N}_{\left(r,s\right)}
\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(w\right)\right)\mathrm{d} w
-\mathsf O_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(u_0,u_1\right)
-\sum_{v\in\mathcal A\setminus\mathcal C}\mathsf Q^{u_0,u_1}_v,
                                                        \label{eq:ud-finite-lower}\\
\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\mathcal C}\left(u\right)
&\leq\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\mathcal C}\left(u_0\right)
+\beta\int_{u_0}^u\eta^{\mathrm{up}}_{\left(r,s\right)}
\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(w\right)\right)\mathrm{d} w
+\mathsf O_{\left(r,s\right)}\left(u_0,u_1\right)
+\sum_{v\in\mathcal A\setminus\mathcal C}\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_v\left(u_0\right).
                                                        \label{eq:ud-finite-upper}
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
These are the unnormalized finite-volume counterparts of Tsai's
(6.5)--(6.6), as used in his (6.32)--(6.35), with the
physical-boundary contributions explicit.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 4: the core--fringe decomposition.}
The core consists of complete blocks with both neighboring blocks in
the finite system; the fringe consists of the remaining boundary pieces.
We prove the result for $m>0$; the case $m<0$ follows by reflection.
By \eqref{eq:ud-support-exhausts}, after discarding finitely many $N$
we may assume that the four central blocks lie in the finite support:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ud-central-buffer}
 A_{b,\mathsf K}\subset\mathcal V_N,\qquad
 b\in\left\{-3/2,-1/2,1/2,3/2\right\}.
\end{equation}
Since $\mathsf K<\infty$ almost surely, the number of discarded systems is
almost surely finite.

For $m>0$, put $m_N=m\wedge i_N^+$. If $m_N\leq0$, the sum is empty. If
$m_N>0$, then $\mathsf D_m^{(N)}=\mathsf D_{m_N}^{(N)}$. Inside
$(0,m_N)\cap\mathbb V$, let $\mathcal C_{N,m}$ be the union of all
complete blocks $A_{b,\mathsf K}$ such that both $A_{b-1,\mathsf K}$ and $A_{b+1,\mathsf K}$
are contained in $\mathcal V_N$, and put
\[
\mathcal E_{N,m}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \left(\left(0,m_N\right)\cap\mathbb V\right)\setminus\mathcal C_{N,m}.
\]
Since $0$ is a block boundary and \eqref{eq:ud-central-buffer} supplies the left neighbor of
the first positive block, every complete block in $(0,m_N)\cap\mathbb V$,
except possibly the last one, has both neighbors contained in $V_N$.
These blocks therefore belong to $\mathcal{C}_{N,m}$. Thus the core is an interval,
possibly empty, and the fringe is covered by at most two blocks: the
last complete block, if excluded from the core, and the block containing
the terminal partial piece, if present. If the target contains no
complete block, it lies entirely within the first positive block.
Consequently,  \eqref{eq:ud-block-size} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ud-fringe-size}
\left|\mathcal E_{N,m}\right|
\leq c_{\kappa,\mathsf K}\left(1+m_N^{1-\kappa}\right).
\end{equation}
In particular, when $m_N=i_N^+$, the block cut by the right physical
endpoint and the adjacent unbuffered complete block are part of the
fringe; no interaction beyond that endpoint is introduced.

By the uniform upper-gap hypothesis
$\sup_{N,v\in\mathcal V_N}l_v^{(N)}<\infty$, equations
\eqref{eq:ud-Q-comparison}, \eqref{eq:ud-common-block-event}, and
\eqref{eq:ud-fringe-size} imply
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ud-fringe-bound}
\sup_{0\leq u\leq T}
\left|\sum_{v\in\mathcal E_{N,m}}
\left(\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_v\left(u\right)-l_v^{\left(N\right)}\right)\right|
\leq \mathsf C_T\left(1+m_N^{1-\kappa}\right).
\end{equation}
Indeed, the left-hand side is at most
$\sum_{v\in\mathcal E_{N,m}}(l_v^{(N)}+\mathsf Q^{0,T}_v)$, and each
fringe piece lies in a block controlled by
\eqref{eq:ud-block-Q-global}.

Suppose the core is nonempty, and denote its first and last block
indices by $b_-$ and $b_+$. For $j=1,\ldots,J$, set
\[
\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lw}}_j\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \left(\mathsf I^-_{b_--1,j},\mathsf I^+_{b_++1,j}\right)\cap\mathbb V,\qquad
\mathcal A^{\mathrm{up}}_j\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \left(\mathsf I^+_{b_--1,j},\mathsf I^-_{b_++1,j}\right)\cap\mathbb V.
\]
Both contain $\mathcal C_{N,m}$ and are contained in $\mathcal V_N$.
Their complements of the core lie in the two neighboring buffer
blocks. Uniformly in $N,m,j$, the block bounds therefore give
\begin{align}
\left|\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lw}}_j\setminus\mathcal C_{N,m}\right|
+\left|\mathcal A^{\mathrm{up}}_j\setminus\mathcal C_{N,m}\right|
&\leq \mathsf C_T\left(1+m_N^{1-\kappa}\right),                            \label{eq:ud-buffer-size}\\
\mathsf O_{\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lw}}_j}\left(t_{j-1},t_j\right)
+\mathsf O_{\mathcal A^{\mathrm{up}}_j}\left(t_{j-1},t_j\right)
&\leq \mathsf C_T\left(1+m_N^{1-\kappa}\right),                            \label{eq:ud-buffer-B}\\
\sum_{v\in\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lw}}_j\setminus\mathcal C_{N,m}}
\mathsf Q^{t_{j-1},t_j}_v
+\sum_{v\in\mathcal A^{\mathrm{up}}_j\setminus\mathcal C_{N,m}}
\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_v\left(t_{j-1}\right)
&\leq \mathsf C_T\left(1+m_N^{1-\kappa}\right).                            \label{eq:ud-buffer-mass}
\end{align}
For the last inequality, also use
$\mathsf L^{(N)}_v(t_{j-1})\leq l_v^{(N)}+\mathsf Q^{0,T}_v$.

It remains to bound the interactions. If
$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{up}}_j=(r,s)\cap\mathbb V$, then
\eqref{eq:ud-mixed-comparison} and \eqref{eq:ud-directed-seeds} imply,
for $u\in[t_{j-1},t_j]$,
\[
\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\left(r,i\right)}\left(u\right)\geq c_*\left(i-r\right)\quad\left(r<i\leq s\right),
\qquad
\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\left(i,s\right)}\left(u\right)\geq c_*\left(s-i\right)\quad\left(r\leq i<s\right).
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ud-upper-interaction}
\eta^{\mathrm{up}}_{\mathcal A^{\mathrm{up}}_j}
\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(u\right)\right)
\leq c_*^{-1}H_{s-r}\leq \mathsf C_T\log\left(2+m_N\right),
\end{equation}
where $H_n=\sum_{q=1}^nq^{-1}$. Here
$s-r=|\mathcal A_j^{\mathrm{up}}|\leq
m_N+\mathsf C_T(1+m_N^{1-\kappa})\leq \mathsf C_T(1+m_N)$ by
\eqref{eq:ud-buffer-size}, which justifies the last bound.

Next write $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lw}}_j=(r,s)\cap\mathbb{V}$ and
$\mathsf Z=\mathsf L^{(N)}_{(r,s)}(u)$. The pointwise estimate
\eqref{eq:ud-Q-comparison}, the initial upper-gap bound, and
\eqref{eq:ud-block-Q-global} apply because
\[
 \left|\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lw}}_j\right|\leq \mathsf C_T\left(1+m_N\right).
\]
Indeed, this interval is contained between the two buffer blocks of
$(0,m_N)$; cover it by the intervening complete blocks and two terminal
fragments. It follows that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ud-z-upper}
\mathsf Z\leq\sum_{v\in\left(r,s\right)}
\left(l_v^{\left(N\right)}+\mathsf Q^{0,T}_v\right)
\leq \mathsf C_T\left(1+m_N\right).
\end{equation}
The outward one-sided bounds and \eqref{eq:ud-mixed-comparison} give
\[
\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\left(i,r\right)}\left(u\right)\geq c_*\left(r-i\right)\quad\left(i_N^-\leq i<r\right),
\qquad
\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\left(s,i\right)}\left(u\right)\geq c_*\left(i-s\right)\quad\left(s<i\leq i_N^+\right).
\]
Insert these bounds in \eqref{eq:ud-eta-lw} and extend both finite
exterior sums to infinity. Then
\begin{align}
\eta^{\mathrm{lw},N}_{\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lw}}_j}
\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(u\right)\right)
&\leq\sum_{q=1}^{\infty}
\frac{\mathsf Z}{\left(\mathsf Z+c_*q\right)c_*q}
=\frac1{c_*}\sum_{q=1}^{\infty}
\left(\frac1q-\frac1{q+\mathsf Z/c_*}\right)                         \notag\\
&\leq\frac1{c_*}\left(1+\log\left(1+\mathsf Z/c_*\right)\right)
\leq \mathsf C_T\log\left(2+m_N\right).                         \label{eq:ud-lower-interaction}
\end{align}
The first inequality also makes explicit why either finite physical
endpoint can only improve this estimate.

Apply \eqref{eq:ud-finite-lower} with
$\mathcal A=\mathcal A^{\mathrm{lw}}_j$ and
\eqref{eq:ud-finite-upper} with
$\mathcal A=\mathcal A^{\mathrm{up}}_j$. Equations
\eqref{eq:ud-buffer-size}--\eqref{eq:ud-lower-interaction} yield
\[
\sup_{t_{j-1}\leq u\leq t_j}
\left|\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\mathcal C_{N,m}}\left(u\right)
-\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_{\mathcal C_{N,m}}\left(t_{j-1}\right)\right|
\leq \mathsf C_T\left(1+m_N^{1-\kappa}+\log\left(2+m_N\right)\right).
\]
The number $J$ depends only on $T,\beta,\rho_*$ and not on $N,m$.
Iterating over $j=1,\ldots,J$, and using
$\log(2+r)\leq C_\kappa(1+r^{1-\kappa})$, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ud-core-bound}
\sup_{0\leq u\leq T}
\left|\sum_{v\in\mathcal C_{N,m}}
\left(\mathsf L^{\left(N\right)}_v\left(u\right)-l_v^{\left(N\right)}\right)\right|
\leq \mathsf C_T\left(1+m_N^{1-\kappa}\right).
\end{equation}
Together with \eqref{eq:ud-fringe-bound}, this proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ud-unscaled-final}
\sup_{0\leq u\leq T}\left|\mathsf D_m^{\left(N\right)}\left(u\right)\right|
\leq \mathsf C_T\left(1+m_N^{1-\kappa}\right),
\qquad m>0,\quad N\text{ sufficiently large}.
\end{equation}

If $m_N\geq1$, then $m_N\leq m$ and $\kappa-1<0$, so
\[
m^{\kappa-1}\left|\mathsf D_m^{\left(N\right)}\left(u\right)\right|
\leq \mathsf C_Tm_N^{\kappa-1}\left(1+m_N^{1-\kappa}\right)\leq2\mathsf C_T.
\]
For $m<0$, reflection gives the same bound with $m_N=m\vee i_N^-$
and absolute values. An empty sum contributes zero.

Finally, only almost surely finitely many $N$ were discarded. For each
such finite system there are only finitely many distinct partial gap
sums, all continuous on $[0,T]$; beyond a physical endpoint the partial
sum is constant while $|m|^{\kappa-1}$ decreases. Their contribution
to the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:uniform-density-error} is therefore
almost surely finite and can be absorbed into $\mathsf C_T$.
For $r\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathsf Z_r$ be the supremum on the left of
\eqref{eq:uniform-density-error} with $T=r$. Continuity permits the time
supremum to be restricted to rational times, so $\mathsf Z_r$ is measurable.
The preceding proof gives $\mathbb{P}[\mathsf Z_r<\infty]=1$. Thus
\begin{equation*}
 \Omega_*\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\bigcap_{r\ge1}\left\{\mathsf Z_r<\infty\right\},\qquad
 \mathsf C_T\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}1+\mathsf Z_{\lceil T\rceil}
\end{equation*}
give a common probability-one event and increasing constants as asserted.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- proposition-24: body_md -->
\label{from inverse of point to inverse of gap}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{theo sde theorem},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:initial-tail-gamma}
 \lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}^{\left(N\right)}\right)+\gamma\right|=0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-24 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
Coordinatewise convergence gives
\begin{equation*}
 C_0\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\sup_N\left|x_0^{\left(N\right)}\right|<\infty.
\end{equation*}
The lower-envelope hypothesis gives deterministic constants $a>0$
and $M_0\in\mathbb N$ such that, whenever the relevant cumulative gap
is finite,
\begin{equation}\label{eq lower bound for l^UN, l}
 l^{\left(N\right)}_{\left(0,\sigma k\right)}\geq ak,
 \qquad \sigma\in\left\{-1,1\right\},\quad k\geq M_0,
\end{equation}
uniformly in $N$; the same estimate holds for $\mathbf{l}$.  Increasing
$M_0$ if necessary, we also have
$|x_{\sigma k}^{(N)}|\geq ak/2$ whenever $\sigma k\in\mathcal I_N$.
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:psi-particle-tail}
 \psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}^{\left(N\right)}\right)
 =-\sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal I_N\\\left|i\right|>M}}
   \frac{1}{x_i^{\left(N\right)}}+e_{N,M},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation*}
 e_{N,M}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} -\sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal I_N\\\left|i\right|>M}}
 \left\{
 \frac{1}{x_i^{\left(N\right)}-x_0^{\left(N\right)}}-\frac{1}{x_i^{\left(N\right)}}
 \right\}
\end{equation*}
and, for $M\geq M_0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:psi-particle-error}
 \left|e_{N,M}\right|
 \leq
 \sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal I_N\\\left|i\right|>M}}
 \frac{\left|x_0^{\left(N\right)}\right|}
 {\left|x_i^{\left(N\right)}\right|\,\left|x_i^{\left(N\right)}-x_0^{\left(N\right)}\right|}
 \leq \frac{C}{M}.
\end{equation}
For $M$ sufficiently large, uniformly for all $N$ after the discarded
initial segment, the particles with $|i|>M$ lie outside $[-b,b]$. Put
\begin{equation*}
 F_{N,M}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal I_N,\ \left|i\right|\leq M\\
                         \left|x_i^{\left(N\right)}\right|>b}}\frac1{x_i^{\left(N\right)}},
 \qquad
 F_M\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sum_{\substack{\left|i\right|\leq M\\\left|x_i\right|>b}}\frac1{x_i}.
\end{equation*}
Then the finite-sum algebra in \eqref{eq:psi-particle-tail}, and its
counterpart for $\mathbf{l}$, reads
\begin{equation*}
 \psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}^{\left(N\right)}\right)
 =-\gamma_{1,b}\left(\mathbf{x}^{\left(N\right)}\right)+F_{N,M}+e_{N,M},
 \qquad
 \psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}\right)=-\gamma_{1,b}\left(\mathbf{x}\right)+F_M+e_M,
\end{equation*}
where $|e_{N,M}|+|e_M|\leq C/M$.  Since $b$ is admissible,
coordinatewise convergence gives $F_{N,M}\to F_M$ for each fixed
$M$, while \eqref{eq def of gamma} gives
$\gamma_{1,b}(\mathbf{x}^{(N)})-\gamma_{1,b}(\mathbf{x})\to\gamma$. Therefore
\begin{equation*}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}^{\left(N\right)}\right)+\gamma-\psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}\right)\right|\leq\frac{C}{M},
 \qquad
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}^{\left(N\right)}\right)+\gamma\right|
 \leq \left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}\right)\right|+\frac{C}{M}.
\end{equation*}
The regular tail estimate
$|\psi_{0,>M}(\mathbf{l})|\leq C M^{-\kappa}$ now proves
\eqref{eq:initial-tail-gamma}.
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{lem:uniform-interaction-tails}
  Under the hypotheses and notation of Theorem \ref{theo sde theorem}, let
$\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{(N)}(\cdot)$ be the finite gap process starting from $\mathbf{l}^{(N)}$.
For every $T>0$, there exist an almost surely finite random integer
$\mathsf M_T$ and an almost surely finite random variable $\mathsf C_T$ such that, almost surely,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:uniform-interaction-tails}
\sup_{N\in\mathbb N}\sup_{t\in\left[0,T\right]}\left|
\psi_{0,>M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{(N)}\left(t\right)\right)-
\psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}^{(N)}\right)\right|\leq \mathsf C_TM^{-\kappa},
\quad M\geq \mathsf M_T.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-72: body_md -->
Work on the common event of Lemma \ref{lem:uniform-density-error} and
fix $T>0$. For $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$ and $k\ge1$, write
$g_{N,k}^{\sigma}=l_{(0,\sigma k)}^{(N)}$ and
$\mathsf G_{N,k}^{\sigma}(t)=\mathsf{L}_{(0,\sigma k)}^{(N)}(t)$.
By \eqref{eq lower bound for l^UN, l} and
\eqref{eq:uniform-density-error}, there are deterministic $a>0$, $M_0$,
and an almost surely finite $\mathsf A_T$ such that, whenever
$g_{N,k}^{\sigma}<\infty$ and $k\ge M_0$,
\begin{equation*}
 g_{N,k}^{\sigma}\ge ak,\qquad
 \left|\mathsf G_{N,k}^{\sigma}\left(t\right)-g_{N,k}^{\sigma}\right|
 \le\mathsf A_Tk^{1-\kappa},\qquad N\in\mathbb N,\quad t\in[0,T].
\end{equation*}
Choose
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf M_T\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} M_0\vee\left\lceil
 \left(2\mathsf A_T/a\right)^{1/\kappa}\right\rceil.
\end{equation*}
For $k\ge\mathsf M_T$, the same bounds give
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf G_{N,k}^{\sigma}\left(t\right)\ge ak/2,\qquad
 \left|\frac1{\mathsf G_{N,k}^{\sigma}\left(t\right)}
       -\frac1{g_{N,k}^{\sigma}}\right|
 \le\frac{2\mathsf A_T}{a^2}k^{-1-\kappa}.
\end{equation*}
The initial and current gap configurations have the same finite support.
If $g_{N,k}^{\sigma}=\infty$, both reciprocals are therefore zero.
Summing over both signs and $k>M$, and using
$\sum_{k>M}k^{-1-\kappa}\le M^{-\kappa}/\kappa$, proves
\eqref{eq:uniform-interaction-tails} with
$\mathsf C_T=4\mathsf A_T/(a^2\kappa)$, uniformly in $N$ and $t\in[0,T]$.
<!-- end proof-72 -->
<!-- proposition-25: body_md -->
\label{prop equation for x_0}
    Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{theo sde theorem}, the finite
    zeroth coordinates converge to the process $\mathsf{X}_0$ given by
    \begin{equation}\label{eq equation for X_0}
        \mathsf{X}_0\left(t\right) = x_0+\mathsf{B}_0\left(t\right) + \frac{\beta}{2}\left(\int_0^t \psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)\mathrm{d} s - \gamma t\right).
    \end{equation}
    Moreover, for any $t>0$, we have, almost surely,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq convergence of X_0}
        \lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{s\in\left[0,t\right]} \left|{\mathsf{X}}_0^{(N)}\left(s\right)-\mathsf{X}_0\left(s\right)\right| =0.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-25 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
Fix $T>0$ and work on an event of probability one on which Corollary
\ref{cor convergence of L^N} and Lemma
\ref{lem:uniform-interaction-tails} hold on $[0,T]$.  Recall from
the gap identity at the beginning of this subsection that
$\mathfrak q(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}^{(N)}(\cdot))=\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{(N)}(\cdot)$.
Consequently,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf{X}_0^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)=x_0^{\left(N\right)}+\mathsf{B}_0\left(t\right)+\frac{\beta}{2}\int_0^t \psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d} s.
\end{equation*}

We first identify the limit of the drift, uniformly on $[0,T]$. For
$M\in\mathbb N$, the core--tail decomposition gives
\begin{equation*}
 \psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)
 =\psi_{0,\leq M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)
 +\psi_{0,>M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right),
\end{equation*}
and the analogous identity holds for $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}$.  For each fixed $M$, Corollary \ref{cor convergence of L^N} gives uniform convergence of every cumulative gap
$\mathsf{L}_{(0,i)}^{(N)}$ with $0<|i|\leq M$.  Since the limiting cumulative
gaps are strictly positive and continuous on $[0,T]$, their minima on
this interval are positive.  Hence
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}
    \sup_{0\leq s\leq T}
    \left|\psi_{0,\leq M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)-\psi_{0,\leq M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)\right|=0.
\end{equation*}

The initial tail is controlled by \eqref{eq:initial-tail-gamma}.
Lemma \ref{lem:uniform-interaction-tails} gives almost surely finite $\mathsf M_T$ and
$\mathsf C_T$ such that, for $M\geq \mathsf M_T$,
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{N\in\mathbb N}\sup_{0\leq s\leq T}
    \left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)
    -\psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}^{\left(N\right)}\right)\right|\leq \mathsf C_TM^{-\kappa}.
\end{equation*}
It follows that
\begin{equation}\label{eq L^N+gamma is closed to l^N+gamma}
    \limsup_{N\to\infty}\sup_{0\leq s\leq T}\left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)+\gamma\right|\leq \mathsf C_TM^{-\kappa}
    +\limsup_{N\to\infty}
    \left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\mathbf{l}^{\left(N\right)}\right)+\gamma\right|.
\end{equation}

We also need the corresponding tail estimate for the limiting gap process.  Put
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf A_T\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sup_{0\leq s\leq T}
    \mathfrak D_{\kappa,\rho}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)<\infty.
\end{equation*}
For all sufficiently large $k$, uniformly in $s\in[0,T]$,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf{L}_{\left(0,\pm k\right)}\left(s\right)\geq\frac{\rho k}{2},
    \quad
    \left|
    \frac{1}{\mathsf{L}_{\left(0,-k\right)}\left(s\right)}
    -\frac{1}{\mathsf{L}_{\left(0,k\right)}\left(s\right)}
    \right|
    \leq\frac{8\mathsf A_T}{\rho^2}k^{-1-\kappa}.
\end{equation*}
Therefore, for all sufficiently large $M$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq psi^M(L(s)) is small}
    \sup_{0\leq s\leq T}
    \left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)\right|
    \leq \mathsf C_T M^{-\kappa}.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\psi_0(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}(\cdot))$ is the uniform limit on $[0,T]$
of the continuous functions $\psi_{0,\leq M}(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}(\cdot))$, and is therefore continuous.

Indeed, the decomposition and the triangle inequality give, for every
$s\leq T$,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
 \left|\psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)-\psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)+\gamma\right|
 \leq{}&\left|\psi_{0,\leq M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)-\psi_{0,\leq M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)\right|\\
 &\quad+\left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)+\gamma\right|
 +\left|\psi_{0,>M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)\right|.
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Taking the supremum in $s$, then the limsup in $N$, and finally letting
$M\to\infty$ in \eqref{eq L^N+gamma is closed to l^N+gamma},
\eqref{eq:initial-tail-gamma}, and
\eqref{eq psi^M(L(s)) is small}, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}
    \sup_{0\leq s\leq T}
    \left|\psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)
    -\psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)+\gamma \right|=0.
\end{equation*}

Let $\mathsf{X}_0$ be the process in the statement.
Since $x_0^{(N)}\to x_0$, the finite-system equation and the uniform
drift convergence give
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{aligned}
    \sup_{0\leq t\leq T}
    \left|\mathsf{X}_0^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)-\mathsf{X}_0\left(t\right)\right|\leq \left|x_0^{\left(N\right)}-x_0\right|+\frac{\beta T}{2}\sup_{0\leq s\leq T}
    \left|\psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)\right)
    -\psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)+\gamma
    \right|\longrightarrow0.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
Thus the limit exists, is uniquely determined by $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}$ and $\mathsf{B}_0$,
and satisfies \eqref{eq equation for X_0}.  Taking a countable intersection over
$T\in\mathbb N$ proves \eqref{eq convergence of X_0} on every compact time interval.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
Define
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf{X}_i\left(t\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} 
 \begin{cases}
  \mathsf{X}_0\left(t\right)+\mathsf{L}_{\left(0,i\right)}\left(t\right),&i>0,\\
  \mathsf{X}_0\left(t\right),&i=0,\\
  \mathsf{X}_0\left(t\right)-\mathsf{L}_{\left(0,i\right)}\left(t\right),&i<0.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation*}
Put
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf{Y}_i\left(t\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \mathsf{X}_i\left(t\right)+\frac{\beta\gamma}{2}t.
\end{equation*}
Then $\mathfrak q(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Y}})=\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}$ and
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf{Y}_0\left(t\right)=x_0+\mathsf{B}_0\left(t\right)
 +\frac\beta2\int_0^t\psi_0\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(s\right)\right)\mathrm{d} s.
\end{equation*}
The gap--particle equivalence in Proposition \ref{ISDE e and u}
therefore shows that $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Y}}$ is the unshifted Dyson ISDE
solution.  Since $\mu_i$ is invariant under common spatial
translations, $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}$ solves \eqref{eq equation for X}.

If $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}}$ is another adapted solution with
gap process in $\mathcal P_{\kappa,\rho}^p$, driven by the same
Brownian family, then
$\widetilde{\mathsf{Y}}_i(t)=\widetilde{\mathsf{X}}_i(t)+\beta\gamma t/2$ is a
second regular solution of the unshifted ISDE.  Proposition
\ref{ISDE e and u} gives $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Y}}}
=\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Y}}$ almost surely, and hence
$\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}}=\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}$.  Finally,
\eqref{eq convergence of X_0} and convergence of every fixed finite
collection of gaps in \eqref{eq convergence of L^N} prove
\eqref{eq convergence of X_i}.  When $\beta=2$, the relation is
$\mathsf{X}_i(t)=\mathsf{Y}_i(t)-\gamma t$, in agreement with Proposition
\ref{gammadependence}.
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- proposition-26: body_md -->
\label{prop s transform convergence}
    Let $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}$, $(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}^{(N)})_{N\geq1}$,
    and $\gamma$ be as in Theorem \ref{theo sde theorem}.  For every
    $T>0$ and compact $\mathcal K\Subset\mathbb H$, almost surely,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq s transform convergence}
       \lim_{N\to\infty} \sup_{t\in\left[0,T\right]}\sup_{z\in\mathcal K}
       \left|\mathsf S_t\left(z\right)+\gamma-\mathsf S^{\left(N\right)}_t\left(z\right)\right|=0.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-26 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
Fix $\mathcal K\Subset\mathbb H$ and work on the common
probability-one event furnished above.  By Proposition
\ref{prop equation for x_0},
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf C_{\mathcal K,T}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sup_N\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\sup_{z\in\mathcal K}
 \left|\mathsf{X}_0^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)-z\right|<\infty.
\end{equation*}
For $N,M\in\mathbb N$, define
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf R_{t,M}^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal I_N\\\left|i\right|>M}}
 \left\{
 \frac1{\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)-z}
 -\frac1{\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)-\mathsf{X}_0^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)}
 \right\}.
\end{equation*}
The mixed comparison with the fixed regular lower process
$\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\mathrm{inf},(N_0)}$ gives random $\mathsf c_T>0$ and $\mathsf M_T<\infty$ such
that, for every $N\geq N_0$, $t\leq T$, and finite coordinate
$i\in\mathcal I_N$ with $|i|\geq \mathsf M_T$,
\begin{equation*}
 \left|\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)-\mathsf{X}_0^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)\right|\geq \mathsf c_T\left|i\right|.
\end{equation*}
The finitely many systems $N<N_0$ can be absorbed by increasing
$\mathsf M_T$.  Increase it again until $\mathsf c_T|i|\geq2\mathsf C_{\mathcal K,T}$ for
$|i|\geq \mathsf M_T$.  The resolvent identity then gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq bd of ep^N_tMz}
 \sup_N\sup_{t\leq T}\sup_{z\in\mathcal K}
 \left|\mathsf R_{t,M}^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)\right|
 \leq 2\mathsf C_{\mathcal K,T}\mathsf c_T^{-2}
 \sum_{\left|i\right|>M}\left|i\right|^{-2}
 \leq\frac{\mathsf C'_{\mathcal K,T}}M.
\end{equation}
Here and below the displayed constants may be random.  Directly from
the definitions,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-S-decomposition}
 \mathsf{S}_t^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)
 =\sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal I_N\\\left|i\right|\leq M}}
 \frac1{\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)-z}
 -\psi_{0,>M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(t\right)\right)
 +\mathsf R_{t,M}^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right).
\end{equation}
The same argument for the regular limiting process gives
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf{S}_t\left(z\right)
 =\sum_{\left|i\right|\leq M}\frac1{\mathsf{X}_i\left(t\right)-z}
 -\psi_{0,>M}\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{L}}\left(t\right)\right)+\mathsf R_{t,M}\left(z\right),
 \qquad
 \sup_{t\leq T,z\in\mathcal K}\left|\mathsf R_{t,M}\left(z\right)\right|\leq\mathsf C/M.
\end{equation*}
For fixed $M$, every label $|i|\leq M$ belongs to $\mathcal I_N$ for
large $N$, and \eqref{eq convergence of X_i} gives uniform convergence
of the finite resolvent sums.  Equations
\eqref{eq:initial-tail-gamma},
\eqref{eq L^N+gamma is closed to l^N+gamma},
\eqref{eq psi^M(L(s)) is small}, and
\eqref{eq bd of ep^N_tMz} control the remaining terms.  Letting first
$N\to\infty$ and then $M\to\infty$ proves
\eqref{eq s transform convergence}.
<!-- end proof-75 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{lemma S^UN SDE}
    For $z\in\mathbb H$, the finite transform $\mathsf{S}_t^{(N)}(z)$
    satisfies
    \begin{equation}\label{eq SDE for S transform}
        \mathrm{d} \mathsf{S}^{(N)}_t\left(z\right) = \mathrm{d} \mathsf{U}^{(N)}_t\left(z\right) + \left(\frac{\beta}{4}\partial_z\left(\mathsf{S}^{(N)}_t\left(z\right)\right)^2+\frac{2-\beta}{4}\partial_z^2\mathsf{S}^{(N)}_t\left(z\right)\right)\mathrm{d} t.
    \end{equation}
    Here, $\mathsf{U}^{(N)}_t(z)$ is a continuous martingale whose bilinear and
    Hermitian covariations are given by
    \begin{equation}\label{eq quadratic variation of sfU}
        \mathrm{d}\left\langle\mathsf{U}^{(N)}\left(z\right),\mathsf{U}^{(N)}\left(z'\right)\right\rangle_t
        =\partial_z\partial_{z'}Q_{\mathsf{S}_t^{(N)}}\left(z,z'\right)\mathrm{d} t,
    \end{equation}
    including $z=z'$ by \eqref{eq:def-Qf}, and
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-hermitian-bracket}
      \mathrm{d}\left\langle\mathsf{U}^{(N)}\left(z\right),\overline{\mathsf{U}^{(N)}\left(w\right)}\right\rangle_t
      =\left.\partial_z\partial_\zeta
      Q_{\mathsf{S}_t^{(N)}}\left(z,\zeta\right)\right|_{\zeta=\overline w}\mathrm{d} t,
    \end{equation}
    where the finite transform in the second variable is continued to
    the lower half-plane by Schwarz reflection.
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-76: body_md -->
Write $I=\mathcal I_N$ and suppress $t$ temporarily.  It\^o's
formula gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq ito for S^UN_t}
\begin{aligned}
 \mathrm{d}\mathsf{S}_t^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)
 &=\left\{
 \sum_{i\in I}\left(\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}-z\right)^{-3}
 -\frac\beta2\sum_{\substack{i,j\in I\\i\neq j}}
 \frac{\left(\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}-z\right)^{-2}}
      {\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}-\mathsf{X}_j^{\left(N\right)}}
 \right\}\mathrm{d} t-\sum_{i\in I}\left(\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}-z\right)^{-2}\mathrm{d}\mathsf{B}_i\left(t\right).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Symmetrizing the finite double sum yields
\begin{equation*}
 \sum_{\substack{i,j\in I\\i\neq j}}
 \frac{\left(\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}-z\right)^{-2}}
      {\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}-\mathsf{X}_j^{\left(N\right)}}
 =-\frac12\partial_z\left(\mathsf{S}_t^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)\right)^2
 +\sum_{i\in I}\left(\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}-z\right)^{-3},
\end{equation*}
where
$\sum_{i\in I}(\mathsf{X}_i^{(N)}-z)^{-3}
=\frac12\partial_z^2\mathsf{S}_t^{(N)}(z)$.  Substitution gives
\eqref{eq SDE for S transform} with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-finite-U}
 \mathsf{U}_t^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} -\int_0^t\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_N}
 \left(\mathsf{X}_i^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)-z\right)^{-2}\mathrm{d}\mathsf{B}_i\left(s\right).
\end{equation}
Taking the bilinear and Hermitian quadratic covariations in
\eqref{eq:def-finite-U} and using the elementary resolvent identity
gives \eqref{eq quadratic variation of sfU} and
\eqref{eq:finite-hermitian-bracket}.
<!-- end proof-76 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{lem:field-ui}
Let $\mathcal K\Subset\operatorname{int}\mathcal K_1$ with
$\mathcal K_1\Subset\mathbb H$, and put
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf A_t\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sup_N\sup_{\substack{0\leq s\leq t\\z\in\mathcal K_1}}
 \left|\mathsf{S}_s^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)\right|,
 \qquad
 \mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \inf\left\{t\leq T:\mathsf A_t\geq R\right\}\wedge T.
\end{equation*}
Then $\mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}$ is a stopping time,
$\mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}\uparrow T$ almost surely, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:field-ui}
 \sup_N\mathbb{E}\left[
  \sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\sup_{z\in\mathcal K}
  \left|\mathsf{U}_{t\wedge\mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)\right|^4
 \right]<\infty.
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds for every fixed finite number of
$z$-derivatives on a smaller compact set.
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-77: body_md -->
Proposition \ref{prop s transform convergence} gives almost sure uniform
convergence of $(\mathsf{S}^{(N)})_N$ on $[0,T]\times\mathcal K_1$. The limit
is continuous, so the family is equicontinuous: uniform convergence
controls the tail, and the finitely many remaining continuous functions
preserve equicontinuity. Hence $\mathsf A_T<\infty$ and $\mathsf A$ is
continuous. Taking the suprema over fixed countable dense subsets
shows that $\mathsf A$ is adapted. Therefore
$\mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}$ is a stopping time and increases to $T$.
Put $\eta=\inf_{z\in\mathcal K_1}\operatorname{Im}z>0$.  Before
$\mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}$,
\begin{equation*}
 \sum_{k\in\mathcal I_N}
 \frac1{\left|\mathsf{X}_k^{\left(N\right)}\left(s\right)-z\right|^4}
 \leq\eta^{-3}\operatorname{Im}\mathsf{S}_s^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)
 \leq\eta^{-3}R.
\end{equation*}
The Burkholder--Davis--Gundy inequality therefore gives, uniformly in
$N$ and $z\in\mathcal K_1$,
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb{E}\left[
  \sup_{t\leq T}\left|\mathsf{U}_{t\wedge\mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)\right|^4
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\eta^{-3}RT\right)^2.
\end{equation*}
Cover $\mathcal K$ by finitely many discs whose doubled closed discs
lie in $\operatorname{int}\mathcal K_1$, and denote the boundary
circles of the doubled discs by $\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_q$.  Cauchy's
formula and H\"older's inequality give
\begin{equation*}
 \sup_{z\in\mathcal K}\left|\mathsf{U}_{t\wedge\mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(z\right)\right|^4
 \leq C_{\mathcal K,\mathcal K_1}
 \sum_{r=1}^q\int_{\Gamma_r}
 \left|\mathsf{U}_{t\wedge\mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\left(N\right)}\left(\zeta\right)\right|^4\left|\mathrm{d}\zeta\right|.
\end{equation*}
Taking the supremum in $t$, then expectation, proves
\eqref{eq:field-ui}.  Cauchy's derivative formula proves the final
assertion.
<!-- end proof-77 -->
<!-- proposition-27: body_md -->
\label{prop:stieltjes-spde}
Fix $\beta\geq1$, $T>0$. Work under the
hypotheses and notation of Theorem \ref{theo sde theorem} and Proposition \ref{prop s transform convergence}, on the
common filtered probability space carrying the Brownian motions
$(\mathsf{B}_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$. Let $\mathsf{S}_t$ be the symmetric Stieltjes
transform of $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}(t)$ on $\mathbb H$.

There exists an adapted field
$\mathsf{U}\in C([0,T];\mathcal O(\mathbb H))$ such that $\mathsf{U}_0=0$ and
$\mathsf{U}(z)$ is a continuous complex local martingale for every
$z\in\mathbb H$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stieltjes-spde}
    \mathsf{S}_{t,\gamma}\left(z\right)
    =
    \mathsf{S}_{0,\gamma}\left(z\right)+\mathsf{U}_t\left(z\right)
    +\int_0^t\mathcal A\left(\mathsf{S}_{s,\gamma}\right)\left(z\right)\,\mathrm{d} s.
\end{equation}
For $z,w\in\mathbb H$, its bilinear and Hermitian covariations are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stieltjes-bilinear-bracket}
    \left\langle\mathsf{U}\left(z\right),\mathsf{U}\left(w\right)\right\rangle_t
    =
    \int_0^t\partial_z\partial_wQ_{\mathsf{S}_s}\left(z,w\right)\,\mathrm{d} s
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stieltjes-hermitian-bracket}
    \left\langle\mathsf{U}\left(z\right),\overline{\mathsf{U}\left(w\right)}\right\rangle_t
    =
    \int_0^t
    \left.
    \partial_z\partial_\zeta Q_{\mathsf{S}_s}\left(z,\zeta\right)
    \right|_{\zeta=\overline w}\mathrm{d} s.
\end{equation}
Finally,
$(\mathsf{S}_{\cdot,\gamma},\mathsf{U})$ satisfies $(\mathbf{SC})$.
<!-- end proposition-27 -->
<!-- proof-78: body_md -->
Recall the finite martingale field from \eqref{eq:def-finite-U}.
Using a countable exhaustion of $\mathbb H$, Proposition \ref{prop s transform convergence} and
Cauchy's integral formula give, on one event of probability one,
\begin{equation*}
    \partial_z^r\mathsf{S}^{(N)}
    \longrightarrow
    \partial_z^r\mathsf{S}_{\cdot,\gamma},
    \quad r=0,1,2,3,
\end{equation*}
locally uniformly on $[0,T]\times\mathbb H$. The finite-system SPDE
therefore yields
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf{U}_t\left(z\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} 
    \mathsf{S}_{t,\gamma}\left(z\right)-\mathsf{S}_{0,\gamma}\left(z\right)
    -\int_0^t\mathcal A\left(\mathsf{S}_{s,\gamma}\right)\left(z\right)\,\mathrm{d} s
\end{equation*}
and $\mathsf{U}^{(N)}\to\mathsf{U}$ in
$C([0,T];\mathcal O(\mathbb H))$.

Use the common localization $\mathsf T_R^{\mathrm{loc}}\uparrow T$
of Lemma \ref{lem:field-ui}, for
$\mathcal K\Subset\operatorname{int}\mathcal K_1$ and
$\mathcal K_1\Subset\mathbb H$. Its fourth-moment bound, together with
$\mathsf{U}^{(N)}\to\mathsf{U}$ in
$C([0,T]\times\mathcal K)$, permits passage to conditional
expectations and proves that the stopped limit is a
$C(\mathcal K)$-valued martingale.  Its fourth-moment bound also gives
uniform integrability of the bilinear and Hermitian compensated
products.  Cauchy's formula for the holomorphic divided differences
gives locally uniform convergence of
$\partial_z\partial_wQ_{\mathsf{S}_s^{(N)}}$ to
$\partial_z\partial_wQ_{\mathsf{S}_s}$, including on the diagonal; the
Hermitian kernels converge in the same way.  Passing to the limit on
a fixed countable dense subset and then using continuity proves that
$\mathsf{U}$ is a local-martingale field and gives
\eqref{eq:stieltjes-bilinear-bracket} and
\eqref{eq:stieltjes-hermitian-bracket}.

For the explicit densities, subtract the symmetric partial sums in
the definition of $\mathsf{S}_s$. Since the constant $\gamma$ cancels,
\begin{equation*}
    Q_{\mathsf{S}_s}\left(z,w\right)
    =
    \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}
    \frac{1}{\left(\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)-z\right)\left(\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)-w\right)}.
\end{equation*}
Membership of $\mathfrak q(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}})$ in $\mathcal{P}_{\kappa,\rho}^p$ implies, uniformly on
compact time intervals,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)
    =
    \mathsf{X}_0\left(s\right)+\rho k+O_T\left(\left|k\right|^{1-\kappa}\right).
\end{equation*}
The series above is therefore absolutely and locally uniformly
convergent away from the poles. Termwise differentiation gives the
bilinear and Hermitian covariance densities
\begin{equation*}
    \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}
    \frac{1}{\left(\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)-z\right)^2\left(\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)-w\right)^2},\quad
    \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}
    \frac{1}{\left(\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)-z\right)^2\left(\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)-\overline w\right)^2},
\end{equation*}
respectively. These series also converge absolutely and locally uniformly
away from the poles.

It remains to verify $(\mathbf{SC})$. Fix $\mathcal D_j$ and
$E_j=\{\mathsf J=j\}$. The same particle asymptotics show that the paired
summands in the Stieltjes series are $O_T(|k|^{-1-\kappa})$, uniformly
on compact time intervals and compact pole-free sets. The series for
its first two derivatives are absolutely and locally uniformly
convergent. Consequently, the selected field $\mathsf W^j$ in the definition of $(\mathbf{SC})$
is adapted, belongs to $C([0,T];\mathcal O(\mathcal D_j))$, and, on
$E_j$, extends continuously to
$[0,T]\times\overline{\mathcal D_j}$. On $\mathcal D_j\cap\mathbb H$,
\eqref{eq:stieltjes-spde} identifies it with
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbf1_{E_j}
    \left\{\mathsf{U}_{t\wedge\mathsf T_{\mathrm{out}}}-\mathsf{U}_{t\wedge\mathsf T_{\mathrm{in}}}\right\}.
\end{equation*}
This is a local martingale because
$\mathbf1_{E_j}\mathbf1_{(\mathsf T_{\mathrm{in}},\mathsf T_{\mathrm{out}}]}$ is predictable.

On $E_j$, put $\mathsf H_t^j=0$ for $t<\mathsf T_{\mathrm{in}}$, and for $t\geq\mathsf T_{\mathrm{in}}$ set
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf H_t^j\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} 
    \sup_{\mathsf T_{\mathrm{in}}\leq u\leq t\wedge\mathsf T_{\mathrm{out}}}
    \sup_{z\in\overline{\mathcal D_j}}
    \left\{
        \left|\mathsf W_u^j\left(z\right)\right|
        +\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\left|\mathsf{X}_k\left(u\right)-z\right|^{-4}
    \right\}.
\end{equation*}
Define
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf T_m^{j,\mathrm{loc}}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \inf\left\{t:\mathsf H_t^j>m\right\}\wedge T.
\end{equation*}
On $E_j^c$, put $\mathsf H^j=0$ and $\mathsf T_m^{j,\mathrm{loc}}=T$. Because
$E_j\in\mathcal F_{\mathsf T_{\mathrm{in}}}$, and because the suprema may be taken over
countable dense sets, $\mathsf T_m^{j,\mathrm{loc}}$ is a stopping time. The
pole-separation assumption and the particle asymptotics give
$\mathsf H_T^j<\infty$, so $\mathsf T_m^{j,\mathrm{loc}}\uparrow T$. For
$0\leq r\leq t\leq T$ and
$A\in\mathcal F_r$, the function
\begin{equation*}
    z\longmapsto
    \mathbb{E}\left[
        \mathbf1_A
        \left\{
            \mathsf W^j_{t\wedge\mathsf T_m^{j,\mathrm{loc}}}\left(z\right)
            -\mathsf W^j_{r\wedge\mathsf T_m^{j,\mathrm{loc}}}\left(z\right)
        \right\}
    \right]
\end{equation*}
is holomorphic by Morera's theorem and dominated convergence. It
vanishes on $\mathcal D_j\cap\mathbb H$, and hence on every component of $\mathcal D_j$
by the identity theorem. Boundedness in the stopped
$C(\mathcal K)$-norm and separability of $C(\mathcal K)$ then give the
$C(\mathcal K)$-valued martingale property for every
$\mathcal K\Subset \mathcal D_j$. Thus $\mathsf W^j$ is a local-martingale field.
Applying the same argument on $\mathcal D_j\times \mathcal D_j$ to the bilinear and
Hermitian compensated products gives the two stopped covariance
formulas; in the Hermitian case the second variable is
anti-holomorphic. Countability of the domains and their components
allows all versions to be chosen simultaneously. This proves
$(\mathbf{SC})$.
<!-- end proof-78 -->
<!-- proposition-28: body_md -->
\label{prop:pole-recovery}
Fix $\beta\geq1$, $\gamma\in\mathbb R$, $p>1$,
$\kappa\in(0,1)$, and $\rho>0$. Let
$(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\geq0},\mathbb{P})$ satisfy the
usual conditions, and let $\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal W$ be deterministic with
$\mathfrak q(\mathbf{x})\in\mathcal L_{\kappa,\rho}^{p}$. Let
$\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}=(\mathsf{X}_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$ be an adapted, coordinatewise
continuous process such that, almost surely,
\begin{equation*}
    \boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}\left(0\right)=\mathbf{x},
    \quad
    \mathsf{X}_i\left(t\right)<\mathsf{X}_{i+1}\left(t\right),
    \quad i\in\mathbb Z,\ t\geq0,
    \quad
    \mathfrak q\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}\right)\in\mathcal{P}_{\kappa,\rho}^p.
\end{equation*}
Let $\mathsf{S}_t$ be the symmetric Stieltjes transform of $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}(t)$.
Suppose there is a single adapted continuous
local-martingale field $\mathsf{U}$ on $\mathbb H$ such that
\eqref{eq:stieltjes-spde},
\eqref{eq:stieltjes-bilinear-bracket},
\eqref{eq:stieltjes-hermitian-bracket}, and $(\mathbf{SC})$ hold on
every compact time interval.

Then there exists an independent family
$(\mathsf{B}_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$ of standard real
$(\mathcal F_t)_{t\geq0}$-Brownian motions such that
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf{X}_i\left(t\right)
    =
    x_i+\mathsf{B}_i\left(t\right)
    +\frac{\beta}{2}\int_0^t
    \left\{\mu_i\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}\left(s\right)\right)-\gamma\right\}\mathrm{d} s,
    \quad i\in\mathbb Z,\ t\geq0.
\end{equation*}
Moreover, $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}$ is the unique strong solution of this
shifted ISDE with initial condition $\mathbf{x}$ among processes whose gap
process belongs to $\mathcal{P}_{\kappa,\rho}^p$.
<!-- end proposition-28 -->
<!-- proof-79: body_md -->
Fix $T>0$ and $i\in\mathbb Z$. Membership in $\mathcal{P}_{\kappa,\rho}^p$ gives,
uniformly for $s\in[0,T]$,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)
    =
    \mathsf{X}_0\left(s\right)+\rho k+O_T\left(\left|k\right|^{1-\kappa}\right).
\end{equation*}
    Hence the paired summands defining $\mu_i(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}(s))$ are
$O_T(|k|^{-1-\kappa})$. Thus the principal value exists locally
uniformly in $s$ and is continuous.  For every compact set
$\mathcal K\Subset\mathbb C\setminus
\bigcup_{0\leq s\leq T}\{\mathsf{X}_k(s):k\in\mathbb Z\}$,
the same estimate gives
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{0\leq s\leq T}\sup_{z\in\mathcal K}
    \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\left|\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)-z\right|^{-4}<\infty.
\end{equation*}

Put $\mathsf T_0=0$. If $\mathsf T_n<T$, let
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf g_n\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} 
    \min\left\{
        \mathsf{X}_i\left(\mathsf T_n\right)-\mathsf{X}_{i-1}\left(\mathsf T_n\right),
        \mathsf{X}_{i+1}\left(\mathsf T_n\right)-\mathsf{X}_i\left(\mathsf T_n\right)
    \right\}.
\end{equation*}
From a fixed enumeration of
$\mathbb Q\times(\mathbb Q_{>0})^2$, select the first
$(\mathsf c_n,\mathsf r_n,\mathsf d_n)$ satisfying the following inequalities, and denote
its enumeration index by $\mathsf J_n$:
\begin{equation*}
    \left|\mathsf c_n-\mathsf{X}_i\left(\mathsf T_n\right)\right|<\frac{\mathsf g_n}{64},
    \quad
    \frac{\mathsf g_n}{4}<\mathsf r_n<\frac{9\mathsf g_n}{32},
    \quad
    \frac{\mathsf g_n}{256}<\mathsf d_n<\frac{\mathsf g_n}{128}.
\end{equation*}
The choice and $\mathsf J_n$ are $\mathcal F_{\mathsf T_n}$-measurable. Define
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
    \mathsf T_{n+1}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} {}&T\wedge\inf\left\{t\geq\mathsf T_n:
        \left|\mathsf{X}_i\left(t\right)-\mathsf c_n\right|\geq \mathsf r_n-2\mathsf d_n
        \text{ or }
        \min_{\varepsilon\in\left\{-1,1\right\}}
        \left|\mathsf{X}_{i+\varepsilon}\left(t\right)-\mathsf c_n\right|
        \leq \mathsf r_n+2\mathsf d_n
    \right\},
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation*}
    \Gamma_n\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \left\{z:\left|z-\mathsf c_n\right|=\mathsf r_n\right\},
    \quad
    D_n\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \left\{z:\mathsf r_n-\mathsf d_n<\left|z-\mathsf c_n\right|<\mathsf r_n+\mathsf d_n\right\},
\end{equation*}
where $\Gamma_n$ is counterclockwise oriented. Throughout
$[\mathsf T_n,\mathsf T_{n+1}]$, $\Gamma_n$ encloses $\mathsf{X}_i$ and no other
pole, and
\begin{equation*}
    \inf_{\substack{\mathsf T_n\leq s\leq\mathsf T_{n+1},\ z\in\overline D_n\\
                    k\in\mathbb Z}}
    \left|z-\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)\right|\geq\mathsf d_n.
\end{equation*}

The construction reaches $T$ after finitely many steps almost surely.
Indeed,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf g_*\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} 
    \min_{0\leq s\leq T}
    \min\left\{
        \mathsf{X}_i\left(s\right)-\mathsf{X}_{i-1}\left(s\right),
        \mathsf{X}_{i+1}\left(s\right)-\mathsf{X}_i\left(s\right)
    \right\}>0.
\end{equation*}
At a nonterminal exit, one of
$\mathsf{X}_{i-1},\mathsf{X}_i,\mathsf{X}_{i+1}$ moves by at least
$7\mathsf g_n/32\geq7\mathsf g_*/32$. Uniform continuity therefore prevents
accumulation of the stopping times. Set $\mathsf T_n=T$ after the first
time that $T$ is reached.

Apply $(\mathbf{SC})$ to the fixed countable family of rational annuli
generated by the preceding enumeration, with $\mathsf T_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathsf T_n$,
$\mathsf T_{\mathrm{out}}=\mathsf T_{n+1}$, and $\mathsf J=\mathsf J_n$ (so $\mathcal D_{\mathsf J_n}=D_n$), and write
$\mathsf V^{(n)}=\mathsf V^{\mathsf T_n,\mathsf T_{n+1}}$. On every event selecting a fixed
rational annulus, contour integration is a continuous linear
functional on $\mathcal O(D_n)$. Hence
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf M_i^{\left(n\right)}\left(t\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} 
    -\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm{i} }
    \oint_{\Gamma_n}z\mathsf V_t^{\left(n\right)}\left(z\right)\mathrm{d} z
\end{equation*}
is a continuous local martingale, stopped on
$[\mathsf T_n,\mathsf T_{n+1}]$. For the random annulus, first localize to the
first $m$ alternatives in the fixed enumeration and use a common localizer for them; letting $m\to\infty$ gives the assertion.

For $\mathsf T_n\leq t\leq\mathsf T_{n+1}$, the residue theorem and the defining
identity for $\mathsf V^{(n)}$ give
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
    \mathsf{X}_i\left(t\right)-\mathsf{X}_i\left(\mathsf T_n\right)
    ={}&\mathsf M_i^{\left(n\right)}\left(t\right)-\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm{i} }
      \int_{\mathsf T_n}^t\oint_{\Gamma_n}
      z\,\mathcal A\left(\mathsf{S}_{s,\gamma}\right)\left(z\right)\mathrm{d} z\mathrm{d} s.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
The uniform pole separation justifies interchanging the time and
contour integrals. Near $\mathsf{X}_i(s)$,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf{S}_{s,\gamma}\left(z\right)
    =
    -\frac{1}{z-\mathsf{X}_i\left(s\right)}+\mathsf h_i\left(s,z\right),
    \quad
    \mathsf h_i\left(s,\mathsf{X}_i\left(s\right)\right)=\gamma-\mu_i\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}\left(s\right)\right).
\end{equation*}
The second identity follows from the locally uniform paired
convergence: the cutoffs centered at $0$ and at $i$ differ by
$2|i|$ boundary terms, each of order $O_T(K^{-1})$. Consequently,
\begin{equation*}
    \frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm{i} }
    \oint_{\Gamma_n}\mathsf{S}_{s,\gamma}\left(z\right)^2\mathrm{d} z
    =2\left\{\mu_i\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}\left(s\right)\right)-\gamma\right\},
    \quad
    \oint_{\Gamma_n}z\,\partial_z^2\mathsf{S}_{s,\gamma}\left(z\right)\mathrm{d} z=0.
\end{equation*}
Using
$\oint_{\Gamma_n}z\,\partial_zf(z)\,\mathrm{d} z
=-\oint_{\Gamma_n}f(z)\,\mathrm{d} z$, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf{X}_i\left(t\right)-\mathsf{X}_i\left(\mathsf T_n\right)
    =
    \mathsf M_i^{\left(n\right)}\left(t\right)
    +\frac{\beta}{2}\int_{\mathsf T_n}^t
    \left\{\mu_i\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}\left(s\right)\right)-\gamma\right\}\mathrm{d} s.
\end{equation*}

Define
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf{B}_i\left(t\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} 
    \mathsf{X}_i\left(t\right)-x_i
    -\frac{\beta}{2}\int_0^t
    \left\{\mu_i\left(\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}\left(s\right)\right)-\gamma\right\}\mathrm{d} s.
\end{equation*}
For each $m$, the process stopped at $\mathsf T_m$ is a finite pasting of
continuous local martingales. Since $\mathsf T_m\uparrow T$ almost surely,
$\mathsf{B}_i$ is a real continuous local martingale on $[0,T]$.

For $i,j\in\mathbb Z$, take a common refinement of their stopping
covers and apply $(\mathbf{SC})$ to the union of the two active annuli.
All unions of two rational annuli form a fixed countable family, and
the selected union is measurable at the left endpoint of each refined
interval.
On a refined interval denote the two active contours by
$\Gamma^{(i)}$ and $\Gamma^{(j)}$.  The bilinear covariance formula
gives
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
    \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} s}\left\langle\mathsf{B}_i,\mathsf{B}_j\right\rangle_s
    ={}&
    \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}
    \left(
        \frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm{i} }
        \oint_{\Gamma^{\left(i\right)}}
        \frac{z\mathrm{d} z}{\left(\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)-z\right)^2}
    \right)
    \left(
        \frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm{i} }
        \oint_{\Gamma^{\left(j\right)}}
        \frac{w\mathrm{d} w}{\left(\mathsf{X}_k\left(s\right)-w\right)^2}
    \right)
    =\delta_{ij}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
The fourth-power bound and Cauchy--Schwarz justify the interchange of
the series and the contour integrals; each contour factor is the
indicator that it encloses $\mathsf{X}_k(s)$. It follows that
\begin{equation*}
    \left\langle\mathsf{B}_i,\mathsf{B}_j\right\rangle_t=\delta_{ij}t.
\end{equation*}
Taking a countable intersection over $T\in\mathbb N$ and
$i,j\in\mathbb Z$ makes these identities simultaneous for all indices
and times. Multidimensional L\'evy's characterization, applied to
every finite subfamily, shows that $(\mathsf{B}_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$ is an
independent family of standard real Brownian motions.

Set $\mathsf{Y}_i(t)=\mathsf{X}_i(t)+\beta\gamma t/2$. Since the gaps and
interaction drift are invariant under a common translation,
$\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Y}}$ is an adapted regular solution of
\eqref{eq ISDE definition} driven by the recovered Brownian family.
Proposition \ref{ISDE e and u} supplies a strong solution driven by that
family, and pathwise uniqueness among adapted regular solutions identifies
it with $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Y}}$. Translating back proves strong existence and
uniqueness for $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}}$.
<!-- end proof-79 -->
